headline: Ukraine hits Russian oil sites with drones

sources.title: Drone offensive hits Russian oil tankers and refineries at 'industrial scale' as Moscow bans diesel exports
Russia bans diesel exports after Ukrainian attacks, straining already tense global market
Russia Bans Diesel Exports to Ensure Domestic Supply After Targeted Ukrainian Drone Strikes

chunks.text: Ukraine {{carried out}} a large drone offensive that lasted about three days. Ukraine said its forces {{stepped up}} attacks on Russian [[oil tankers]] and [[refineries]]. One Ukrainian commander described the campaign as reaching an "industrial scale." According to reports, the [[drones]] {{set off}} fires at several energy sites, and Ukraine claimed it had hit 21 [[vessels]], including 19 oil tankers, near Crimea.

verbs.correct: To do or complete a planned task or action

verbs.wrong: To aim at more important targets
verbs.correct: To increase or intensify an activity

verbs.wrong: To destroy something in an explosion
verbs.correct: To cause something to start suddenly

chunks.text: The strikes {{knocked out}} part of Russia's oil production. According to reports, the Omsk [[refinery]] in Siberia, which is Russia's largest, {{shut down}} some operations after it was hit. The plant sits about 1,700 miles from Ukrainian territory and normally makes around 460,000 [[barrels]] of [[fuel]] a day. Two industry sources said work at the site stopped for a time.

verbs.wrong: To reduce something to half its size
verbs.correct: To destroy or stop something from working

verbs.wrong: To move work to a safer place

chunks.text: Inside Russia, the attacks led to serious [[fuel shortages]]. Long lines {{built up}} at [[gas stations]] in several regions, and some areas {{brought in}} limits on how much fuel drivers could buy. Prices {{went up}} quickly. One Russian official said the situation at filling stations was "causing concern" among the public, and reports said some stations {{ran out}} of [[gasoline]].

chunks.text: In response, Russia {{hit back}} at the pressure on its fuel market by cutting exports. Russian officials said they would {{hold back}} [[diesel]] [[exports]] until July 31 to keep enough fuel at home. To {{deal with}} the shortages, reports said Russia planned to buy fuel from other countries and had already started importing gasoline from India. Analysts said the [[export ban]] could push global diesel prices higher.

tf.s: Ukraine carried out a large drone offensive that lasted about three days.
tf.why: Ukraine carried out (did) the planned offensive. This matches what happened.

tf.s: As fuel became hard to find, prices went down across Russia.
tf.why: Prices went up (rose) during the shortage. Go down means to fall, which is the opposite of what happened.

tf.s: To deal with the shortages, Russia planned to buy fuel from other countries.
tf.why: Russia moved to deal with (handle) the shortages by importing fuel. This is correct.

tf.s: Inside Russia, some gas stations ran out of gasoline during the shortages.
tf.why: The stations ran out (had none left) of gasoline. This matches the reports.

tf.s: Ukraine called off its attacks on Russian oil tankers and refineries.
tf.why: Ukraine stepped up (increased) its attacks. Call off means to cancel, which is not what happened.

tf.s: Russia stepped up its diesel exports until the end of July.
tf.why: Russia held back (stopped) its diesel exports. Step up means to increase, which is the opposite of what happened.
